The '''Mary P. Dolciani Award''' is an award established in 2012 by the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Dolciani Award|url=https://maa.org/the-mary-p-dolciani-award/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Mathematical Association of America}}</ref> The award recognizes a pure or applied mathematician with a record of distinguished contributions to K-16 mathematics education in the United States or Canada and comes with a $5,000 award.<ref name=":0" /> Examples of significant contributions include, but are not limited to, the development of K-16 mathematics curriculum, educational technology, or programs to improve teaching or teacher preparation.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Dolciani Award Guidelines|url=https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/research-awards/dolciani-award/dolciani-award-guidelines|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Mathematical Association for America}}</ref> The prize is funded by a grant established by mathematician, educator, and author [[Mary P. Dolciani]], who dedicated her career to improving mathematics education and is the author of several secondary- and college-level mathematics textbooks.{{Citation needed|date=August 2022}}

It should be distinguished from the Mary P. Dolciani Prize for Excellence in Research, awarded beginning in 2019 by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=38|title=Mary P. Dolciani Prize for Excellence in Research|work=Prizes and awards|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=2020-10-28}}</ref>
